subject: Capacity planning: token bandwidth & p95 latency targets
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Alex Cho <alex.cho@entraxis.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity planning: token bandwidth & p95 latency targets

Alex —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. As promised I attached a quick token profile template (entraxis_token_profile.csv) — could you fill in the typical prompt/response lengths and estimated concurrent active users for weekdays vs. weekends? That will let us model tokens/sec and p95 latency under three scenarios: baseline (current usage), growth (3-6 months), and peak stress (marketing spike).

High-level asks from our side:
- Confirm traffic mix (chat vs. single-turn generation) and average tokens per request.
- Any hard p95 latency targets for synchronous user-facing requests? You mentioned ~300–350ms as a goal earlier — confirm.
- Call out any regions where low latency matters more (we assume us-west primary).

We'll run an initial GPU provisioning simulation (tokens/sec -> GPUs needed) and provide recommended slab sizes and headroom assumptions (10/25/50% scenarios). Ben will look at fallback model variants (quantized vs. full fp16) for aggressive cost tradeoffs.

Next step: return the CSV by EOD Wednesday and we'll follow up with a short modeling note and a proposed Dedicated slab.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

Kimberly —

Thanks, attached is a filled token profile with week/day breakdown and a sample of our prompt/response pairs. Key notes:
- 70% chat flows (multi-turn, avg 110 tokens in, 220 tokens out), 30% single-shot completions (avg 20 in, 60 out).
- Concurrent active users: baseline 350, growth 1,100, peak marketing spike estimate 4,500 (short duration).
- SLO: p95 <= 350ms for text chat in US-west. Can tolerate up to 700ms for non-interactive batch jobs.
- Preferred models: accuracy-sensitive flows should run on the full fp16 variant, fallback to q4_0 quantized for lower-cost routes.

We also included a sample QPS distribution by hour — see the CSV. Maya copied for ops visibility.

Alex

On Wed, Jul 7, 2027 at 11:37 AM Alex Cho <alex.cho@entraxis.ai> wrote:
> Kimberly —
>
> Thanks, attached is a filled token profile with week/day breakdown and a sample of our prompt/response pairs. Key notes:
> - 70% chat flows (multi-turn, avg 110 tokens in, 220 tokens out), 30% single-shot completions (avg 20 in, 60 out).
> - Concurrent active users: baseline 350, growth 1,100, peak marketing spike estimate 4,500 (short duration).
> - SLO: p95 <= 350ms for text chat in US-west. Can tolerate up to 700ms for non-interactive batch jobs.
> - Preferred models: accuracy-sensitive flows should run on the full fp16 variant, fallback to q4_0 quantized for lower-cost routes.

Alex / Kimberly —

Thanks for the data. I ran a quick back-of-envelope simulation and attached a more detailed capacity model (redwood_capacity_model_v2.xlsx). Highlights up front:

- Token-rate conversions: with the mix you provided, baseline tokens/sec at peak hour is ~62k tok/s, growth ~195k tok/s, marketing spike ~800k tok/s (short burst). Those are aggregate across all routes.

- GPU sizing (initial suggestion, US-west):
  * Baseline: 4 x A100 80GB-equivalent slots (with 15% headroom) running fp16 model variants; estimated p95 ~320ms.
  * Growth: 12 x A100-equivalent slots (25% headroom), split across two availability zones for redundancy; p95 ~340–360ms depending on prefix cache hit rates.
  * Spike: short-term burst requires ~45 x A100-equivalent slots to keep p95 under 350ms if everything routes to full fp16. If we accept progressive fallback to q4_0 for <20% of requests, required capacity drops to ~30 slots.

- Ops knobs that materially change headroom: batching window (50–150ms), KV/prefix cache hit rate (warm caches reduce effective tokens/sec by ~18–30%), and early-exit/length truncation for non-critical completions.

Action items for model accuracy vs cost trade:
- Define which endpoints must never fall back to quantized variants (we'll mark those as "accuracy-critical").
- Agree on a short-term burst policy: do we pre-provision burst capacity (reserved) or rely on cross-tenant soft capacity + auto-fallback? (Reserved preferred for guarantees).

I'll walk through the workbook in a 30m call if useful. Kimberly — can you propose times today? Also pinging Aditya to validate the slot-equivalence assumptions and potential use of T4/GPU-mix for non-critical workloads.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Director, Solutions Architecture, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Alex / team —

Great — thanks for the quick turnaround and Ben's modeling note. Two quick clarifications before we lock in the proposed Dedicated slab:

1) Headroom target: EntraXis, do you want us to price for a 25% committed headroom (recommended for predictable user-facing SLOs) or a leaner 10% to reduce monthly spend and accept higher fallback risk?

2) Burst policy: we can offer a 30-day burst commit (prepaid buffer) that Redwood will reserve for you during known campaigns (marketing spikes). If you prefer not to prepay, we can design a policy combining reserved baseline + auto-fallback tiers that soft-enables cross-tenant absorbency but cannot be SLA-backed. Which do you prefer?

Next steps I propose:
- Alex: confirm headroom percentage and whether burst buffer will be prepaid.
- Ben/Aditya: finalize the A100-equivalent slot counts and provide line items for Reserved slab pricing vs. hybrid reserved+burst pricing.
- Kimberly: draft an updated mutual action plan and delivery timeline once numbers are confirmed.

Available to jump on a quick call at 4:30pm PT today to finalize if that's good for you.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
